instructions: Establish a clear tonal hierarchy to define the subject against the background, ensuring the focal point is visually dominant. Prioritize a strong, recognizable silhouette by concentrating on the outline and key distinctive features. Utilize negative space intentionally to separate elements and enhance readability. Apply shading and texture strategically to create depth and volume, avoiding flat uniformity. Ensure the spatial layout balances the subject with its surroundings to maintain visual clarity and impact.

candidates.draw: Compose a large, recognizable focal subject with clear silhouette and distinctive features; use negative space and intentional shading.

Establish a solid, uninterrupted silhouette to anchor the composition; ensure the subject’s outline is distinct from the background. Define key features with high-contrast characters to prevent visual ambiguity, especially for small details like eyes or beaks that must remain legible at low resolution. Use intentional negative space around the focal point to enhance readability and reduce clutter. Apply tonal hierarchy by varying character density—use sparse, lighter textures for background areas and dense, darker patterns for core mass and shadows. Prioritize structural clarity over intricate detail, ensuring spatial relationships between elements are immediately apparent.
